purpose: Teach: ジャングル/大谷/月日/レンタカー/横須賀/姓/細工/繁華

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、テレビで、ジャングルの探検番組、本当に、夢中になって、見たよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?あの番組、家族で、観たよな。
lines.en: When I was young, I used to watch this jungle exploration show on TV, remember? We'd all gather around and watch it together. You remember that, don't you?
lines.style: Soft, unhurried opening. Voice carries the weight of old memory — not sad, but tender with distance. Reaches toward her at the end, inviting her into the moment together.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。最近の野球選手、大谷さんって、本当に、すごい選手ね、テレビで、活躍、見るたびに、ワクワクするわよね、あなたも、好きでしょ?
lines.en: Yes. That Otani fellow, the baseball player lately — he's really something, isn't he? Every time I see him on TV doing his thing, I get that little spark of joy. You like him too, don't you?
lines.style: Bright, engaged. Quick rhythm on the words about Otani — genuine enthusiasm breaking through. Warm turn toward him at the end, drawing him into her delight.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 結婚してから、もう、相当な、月日、経ったよな、ばあさん、本当に、ありがたいよ、ここまで、共に、過ごしてくれて、感謝、しないとな。
lines.en: It's been quite a long time since we got married. So much time has passed. I'm really grateful for it, you know. For us going through all of it together. I need to thank you for that.
lines.style: Quiet, sincere opening. Breath catches slightly on 'grateful.' Slow pace — each phrase distinct, deliberate. Voice settles lower, almost a prayer in tone. Eye-level intimacy.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、二人で、レンタカー、借りて、旅行、よく、行ったわよね、覚えてる、あなた、楽しい、思い出ね、本当に、また、行きたいね。
lines.en: When we were young, we'd rent a car the two of us and go on trips all the time, remember? Such happy memories. I wish we could do that again.
lines.style: Wistful, almost dreaming. Voice softens on 'remember' — checking if he's there with her in it. Slight lift at 'happy' before drifting into longing at the end. Reaches gently for the past.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、横須賀、出張で、行ったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる、あの頃の私、本当に、忙しかったわよな、家族、寂しい思い、させちゃったよな。
lines.en: I went to Yokosuka on a business trip back then, didn't I? You remember? I was terribly busy in those days. I'm sorry — I made things lonely for the family.
lines.style: Regretful undertone beneath calm surface. Voice tightens slightly on the admission. Quiet, almost to himself. Not seeking reassurance, but sitting with the weight of old absence.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、お父さんの姓を、新しく、いただいて、ちょっと、慣れるのに、時間、かかったわよね、私、覚えてる、不思議な気持ちだったわ、新しい姓。
lines.en: I remember when I took your family name. It was new to me, and I needed time to get used to it. That strange feeling — becoming someone with a new name.
lines.style: Wondering, almost marveling. Slight pause before 'new name.' Voice carries the echo of who she was before — tender without melancholy. Softly introspective, like she's still a little amazed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、私、木の細工、結構、得意だったわよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?家族に、いろいろ、作ってあげたよな、楽しかったわよな、本当に。
lines.en: I was quite good at woodworking when I was younger, wasn't I? You remember? I made all sorts of things for the family. It was so much fun back then, really.
lines.style: Gentle pride mixed with wistfulness. Slight brightness on 'good' — not boasting, just stating a forgotten fact. Fades into fondness at the end. Like holding something delicate in the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔の繁華街、本当に、賑やかだったわよね、覚えてる、あなた、夜店、いっぱい、出ていたのよ、夏祭り、楽しかったわね、二人で、よく、行ったね。
lines.en: The old town was so lively back then, wasn't it? All those little stalls at night, especially during the summer festivals. We used to go together so often. Those were good times.
lines.style: Warm and close. Voice comes alive remembering the crowds, the summer air. Slight acceleration on 'stalls' — painting the scene. Gentle landing at 'together,' drawing him into shared time.
